run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation application came up cleanly at 2026-11-21T14:46:15Z, but its entry-point Service `frontend` (hotel-reservation) was left with a selector that matches a pod which does not serve port 5000: the live Service selects service-route=frontend (its own applied manifest says io.kompose.service=frontend), and exactly two pods carry that label - frontend-5566ddfbfb-rmmll and search-9cd459687-w7qtr. The resulting Endpoints object for `frontend` lists both pods on port 5000, while the search process listens only on 8082/9092, so connections the frontend Service load-balances onto the search pod are refused. Observed consequences at 14:46:50Z: kube_endpoint_address_available{endpoint="frontend"}=2 for a single-port Service fronted by a 1-replica Deployment, the blackbox TCP probe to frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 returned 0 (0.0023 s, immediate refusal) while the exporter scrape itself was up, the frontend pod itself still answered HTTP GET /hotels with 200 in ~4-5 ms, and the ServiceEndpointDown alert fired for deployment frontend. Rollout events show config-only re-rolls of the frontend and search Deployments at 14:46:29-14:46:33 with the same image digest, and resourceVersion order places the pod-template label writes (frontend Deployment 184408, search Deployment 184455) just before the Service selector write (184456). The application internals checked show no errors: rate 1001/1001 requests completed with 0 rejected/expired, search 72/72 rate calls successful with 0 failures/timeouts, zero container restarts, and both mongo-backed services authenticated as `admin`, with no sign that the privilege-revocation scripts in the failure-admin-geo/failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps were executed. Only ~35 s of telemetry exist (all pods, Prometheus and Jaeger start 14:46:15-14:46:50), so pre-incident state and the actor that applied the changes are not observable. Four other TCP probes (geo, rate, reservation, search) also read 0 in the same single sample and are left as an unexplained gap rather than declared impact.

claims.text: The live `frontend` Service in namespace hotel-reservation has spec.selector={"service-route":"frontend"}, while its kubectl last-applied-configuration declares selector {"io.kompose.service":"frontend"}; the Service was created at 2026-11-21T14:46:15Z and last written at resourceVersion 184456.

The Endpoints object of Service `frontend` exposes two addresses on port 5000: frontend-5566ddfbfb-rmmll (10.244.234.189, node sregym-worker) and search-9cd459687-w7qtr (10.244.125.55, node sregym-worker3).
Exactly two pods in hotel-reservation carry the label service-route=frontend: frontend-5566ddfbfb-rmmll and search-9cd459687-w7qtr; no other pod in the namespace carries it.

Deployment `search` (generation 2) has pod-template labels {io.kompose.service: search, service-route: frontend} while its applied manifest lists only io.kompose.service: search; Deployment `frontend` (generation 2) likewise carries service-route: frontend in its pod template although its manifest lists only io.kompose.service: frontend.

The search container serves only gRPC port 8082 (plus metrics 9092): its startup log reads "Read target port: 8082", and the search Deployment declares containerPort 8082 and 9092 only - nothing listens on port 5000, the port the `frontend` Service targets.

At 2026-11-21T14:46:50Z kube_endpoint_address_available{namespace="hotel-reservation",endpoint="frontend"}=2, i.e. the single-port frontend Service has two endpoint addresses, while the frontend Deployment has replicas=1 and other single-port hotel-reservation Services report 1 (rate and search report 2 because each Endpoints declares two named ports).

The blackbox tcp_connect probe for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 returned probe_success=0 at 2026-11-21T14:46:50Z with probe_duration_seconds≈0.0023 s (immediate refusal, not a timeout), while up{job="blackbox-hotel-reservation"}=1 for that target, so the probe result is a genuine failed connection through the frontend Service.

The frontend pod itself was healthy in the same period: span rows returned for service frontend show HTTP GET /hotels with http.status_code=200 at durations ~3.6-5.3 ms and HTTP GET /recommendations 200, with start_us 1795272409.75-1795272409.99 (≈2026-11-21T14:46:49.8Z) and no error flag on those rows.

The alert ServiceEndpointDown (severity critical) is recorded as pending for deployments frontend, geo, rate, reservation and search in hotel-reservation at the end of the window, and the alerting rule's own state shows the frontend instance frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 firing (activeAt 2026-11-21T14:46:49Z) with value 0; the rule matches probe_success==0 for endpoints whose deployment has replicas available.

The frontend and search Deployments were re-rolled with unchanged pod images at 14:46:29-14:46:33Z: ReplicaSet frontend-5566ddfbfb created 14:46:29 and frontend-68745cb99c deleted 14:46:31, ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 created 14:46:31 and search-567bb6c4b8 scaled 1→0 at 14:46:33; all hotel-reservation app pods use the same image digest ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation:sha-d2c036bc3…, matching a configuration-only (label) rollout.

Write ordering from resourceVersion shows the label/selector changes as one sequence: frontend Deployment rv 184408 → search Deployment rv 184455 → frontend Service rv 184456, i.e. the Service selector was written last, after the two pod templates were labelled.

Application-level counters show no internal failures at 14:46:50Z: rate exposes rate_requests_received_total=1001, rate_requests_completed_total=1001, rate_requests_rejected_total=0, rate_requests_expired_total=0, rate_queue_depth=0, rate_backend_qps_limit=500; search exposes search_requests_total=72, search_rate_attempts_total=72, search_rate_successes_total=72, search_rate_failures_total=0, search_rate_timeouts_total=0.

All 19 hotel-reservation pods are Running and ready with restart count 0, pod start times 14:46:15-14:46:31Z, and no waiting/terminated container reasons are present, so no crash, OOMKill or eviction explains the failure.

The mongo-backed rate and geo services authenticate successfully as principal `admin`: mongodb-rate logged Authentication succeeded for admin at 14:46:26, 14:46:30 and 14:46:48 from 10.244.125.37 (the rate pod), and mongodb-geo logged Authentication succeeded for admin at 14:46:23 followed by createCollection and an index build on geo-db.geo.

The frontend Service's selector change is what produces the failure: with selector service-route=frontend the Service's endpoint set contains a pod (search-9cd459687-w7qtr) whose process listens only on 8082/9092, so connections addressed to the frontend ClusterIP port 5000 can be refused even though the frontend pod serves 200s; this is the only Service in the namespace whose selector does not match its own workload's io.kompose.service label.

Alternative attribution of the same injected change: if the fault is catalogued as a mislabelled workload rather than a bad Service selector, the fault-holding object would be Deployment `search` in hotel-reservation, whose pod template gained service-route: frontend (generation 2) and thereby joined the frontend Service's endpoints; the Service selector write (rv 184456) came after that label write (rv 184455), so both objects are part of one injection and only the attribution differs.

An additional, unexplained connectivity problem may affect geo.hotel-reservation:8083, rate.hotel-reservation:8084, reservation.hotel-reservation:8087 and search.hotel-reservation:8082: their tcp_connect probes also read probe_success=0 at 14:46:50Z (durations 0.002-0.004 s, exporter up=1) although their endpoints had 1-2 available addresses and their processes were serving; this rests on a single sample and no pod-level error evidence was found for these four services.

A MongoDB admin-privilege fault on geo-db or rate-db was considered and rejected for this window: the failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps (holding remove-admin-mongo.sh / revoke-admin-*.sh scripts) are mounted at /scripts in the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate Deployments, but no execution banner, revoke or authentication failure appears in the mongo logs, and both databases accepted `admin` logins at 14:46:23-14:46:48 with successful writes.

The continuously failing HTTP probe blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation (probe_success=0 and probe_http_status_code=0 at every 15 s sample from 14:45:00 to 14:46:45) was considered as user-facing impact and rejected as evidence about this application: the probe target is ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx, and the queried namespace list and Ingress query show no ingress-nginx namespace and no Ingress objects in this cluster, so that probe measures a non-existent path.

Restore the frontend Service to a single correct endpoint: set Service `frontend` spec.selector back to io.kompose.service: frontend (or remove service-route: frontend from the search Deployment pod template, keeping the templates consistent), then verify kube_endpoint_address_available{endpoint="frontend"}=1 and probe_success{instance="frontend.hotel-reservation:5000"}=1.

Decide whether the /scripts failure-script mounts (ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate) should remain on the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate Deployments; they carry dropUser/revokeRolesFromUser scripts for the `admin` user on geo-db and rate-db and are the only fault-injection artefacts found that are not in the workloads' applied manifests.

gaps: Only about 35 seconds of telemetry exist inside the authorized window: all 19 hotel-reservation pods, Prometheus and Jaeger start at 2026-11-21T14:46:15-14:46:50Z, and every queried metric series has a single sample at 14:46:50Z, so there is no pre-incident baseline and no way to see how long the Service selector/label changes had been in effect or whether the alert condition predates the window.

The actor and exact timestamps of the three configuration writes (frontend Deployment pod labels rv 184408, search Deployment pod labels rv 184455, frontend Service selector rv 184456) are not observable: the change_history integration is not available, no Kubernetes Event records an Update of a Service or Deployment template, and Secrets cannot be read.

The trace search for error-tagged spans (tags error=true) for frontend and for search over 14:30:00-14:46:50Z returned no rows (status no_data); that shows only that the query matched nothing and is not used as evidence that no errors occurred.

The Loki queries for error-like lines in hotel-reservation between 14:46:30 and 14:46:50Z and for ingress-nginx lines mentioning the search pod returned no rows (status no_data), so the absence of post-rollout application error lines is unchecked rather than proven.

The Prometheus instant query for traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="hotel-reservation"} returned no rows (status no_data), so per-service error-rate and request-rate breakdowns from span metrics are unavailable for the window.

Whether the four other blackbox tcp_connect failures at 14:46:50Z (geo:8083, rate:8084, reservation:8087, search:8082) persisted is unknown: each target has exactly one probe sample in the window; their endpoints had available addresses and their application counters/logs show no errors, so they are recorded as unexplained rather than as impact.

Client-visible failure of /hotels-style requests could not be measured directly: there is no ingress-nginx controller or Ingress object in this cluster, no locust metrics job for hotel-reservation, and refused connections never produce application spans; a kube-state-metrics series for load-generator pod wrk2-job-77m9f exists but that pod is no longer present, so its request/failure data is unavailable.

Search-log lines showing consul 'connection refused' at 14:46:16-14:46:21 come from the startup phase before the consul Service had endpoints; no post-startup consul resolution errors were seen, but Loki returns only a limited number of the newest lines, so this check is not exhaustive.

Two views used here are marked incomplete: the frontend span slice (60 of 219 rows) and the mongo/rate log reads (newest 20 of 26 and newest 60 of 203 matching lines), so statements about those logs and spans describe the rows shown only.
next_steps: Revert the hotel-reservation `frontend` Service selector to io.kompose.service=frontend (rolling back the last write, resourceVersion 184456) and re-check that the Endpoints object lists only frontend-5566ddfbfb-*:5000.
Remove the injected service-route: frontend label from the search Deployment pod template so no non-frontend pod can join the frontend Service's endpoint set.

Add a guard on endpoint count versus Deployment replica count for single-port Services (kube_endpoint_address_available vs kube_deployment_spec_replicas) so a mis-selected Service is detected without relying on TCP probes.

Decide and document the disposition of the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate script mounts on the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate Deployments, and confirm out-of-band that the `admin` user still holds readWrite on geo-db and rate-db.

Re-inspect the geo, rate, reservation and search blackbox probes once more telemetry is available to determine whether their 14:46:50Z failures were a startup artefact or a second independent problem.

content:
global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:
- job_name: kube-state-metrics
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - action: drop
    regex: chaos-mesh|khaos
    source_labels:
    - namespace
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: .*kube-state-metrics.*
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoints_name
- job_name: prometheus-self
  static_configs:
  - targets:
    - localhost:9090
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-cadvisor
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - action: drop
    regex: chaos-mesh|khaos
    source_labels:
    - namespace
  relabel_configs:
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/${1}/proxy/metrics/cadvisor
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
    insecure_skip_verify: true
- job_name: node-exporter
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoints_name
# ---- Blackbox TCP probes for app service endpoints ----
# Probes each service's ClusterIP:port via the blackbox exporter.

- job_name: 'blackbox-astronomy-shop'
  metrics_path: /probe
  params:
    module: [tcp_connect]
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - ad.astronomy-shop:8080
        - cart.astronomy-shop:8080
        - checkout.astronomy-shop:8080
        - currency.astronomy-shop:8080
        - email.astronomy-shop:8080
        - frontend.astronomy-shop:8080
        - frontend-proxy.astronomy-shop:8080
        - image-provider.astronomy-shop:8081
        - payment.astronomy-shop:8080
        - product-catalog.astronomy-shop:8080
        - product-reviews.astronomy-shop:3551
        - quote.astronomy-shop:8080
        - recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080
        - shipping.astronomy-shop:8080
        - flagd.astronomy-shop:8013
        - kafka.astronomy-shop:9092
      labels:
        namespace: astronomy-shop
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__address__]
      target_label: __param_target
    - source_labels: [__param_target]
      target_label: instance
    - target_label: __address__
      replacement: prometheus-prometheus-blackbox-exporter:9115

- job_name: 'blackbox-hotel-reservation'
  metrics_path: /probe
  params:
    module: [tcp_connect]
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - frontend.hotel-reservation:5000
        - search.hotel-reservation:8082
        - profile.hotel-reservation:8081
        - geo.hotel-reservation:8083
        - rate.hotel-reservation:8084
        - recommendation.hotel-reservation:8085
        - user.hotel-reservation:8086
        - reservation.hotel-reservation:8087
      labels:
        namespace: hotel-reservation
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__address__]
      target_label: __param_target
    - source_labels: [__param_target]
      target_label: instance
    - target_label: __address__
      replacement: prometheus-prometheus-blackbox-exporter:9115

- job_name: 'hotel-reservation-application'
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - search.hotel-reservation:9092
        - rate.hotel-reservation:9091
      labels:
        namespace: hotel-reservation

- job_name: 'blackbox-social-network'
  metrics_path: /probe
  params:
    module: [tcp_connect]
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - nginx-thrift.social-network:8080
        - media-frontend.social-network:8081
        - user-service.social-network:9090
        - compose-post-service.social-network:9090
        - social-graph-service.social-network:9090
        - post-storage-service.social-network:9090
        - user-timeline-service.social-network:9090
        - url-shorten-service.social-network:9090
        - text-service.social-network:9090
        - unique-id-service.social-network:9090
        - user-mention-service.social-network:9090
        - home-timeline-service.social-network:9090
        - media-service.social-network:9090
      labels:
        namespace: social-network
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__address__]
      target_label: __param_target
    - source_labels: [__param_target]
      target_label: instance
    - target_label: __address__
      replacement: prometheus-prometheus-blackbox-exporter:9115
# ---- Ingress HTTP probes ----
- job_name: 'blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation'
  metrics_path: /probe
  params:
    module: [http_2xx]
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=2015-04-09&outDate=2015-04-10&lat=38.0235&lon=-122.095
      labels:
        namespace: hotel-reservation
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__address__]
      target_label: __param_target
    - source_labels: [__param_target]
      target_label: instance
    - target_label: __address__
      replacement: prometheus-prometheus-blackbox-exporter:9115

# ---- Locust load generator metrics ----
- job_name: 'locust-astronomy-shop'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - load-generator.astronomy-shop:9646
      labels:
        namespace: astronomy-shop

- job_name: 'locust-train-ticket'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - load-generator.train-ticket:9646
      labels:
        namespace: train-ticket

# ---- OTel Collector spanmetrics (Jaeger traces) ----
- job_name: 'otel-spanmetrics'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - otel-collector.observe:8889
  metric_relabel_configs:
    # Strip "unknown_service:" prefix and "_process" suffix from blueprint-hotel-reservation service names
    # e.g. unknown_service:frontend_service_process -> frontend_service
    - source_labels: [service_name]
      regex: 'unknown_service:(.+)_process'
      target_label: service_name
      replacement: '$1'
    # Drop wlgen metrics — not a real service
    - source_labels: [service_name]
      regex: 'unknown_service:wlgen_proc'
      action: drop
    # Use the namespace attached to the trace, not a service-name guess.
    - source_labels: [k8s_namespace_name]
      regex: '(.+)'
      target_label: namespace
      replacement: '$1'

# ---- OTel Collector spanmetrics (OTLP traces) ----
- job_name: 'otel-spanmetrics-otlp'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - otel-collector.observe:8890
  metric_relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [k8s_namespace_name]
      regex: '(.+)'
      target_label: namespace
      replacement: '$1'
# ---- Scraping from TiDB Cluster ----
- job_name: tidb-cluster
  scrape_interval: 15s
  metrics_path: /metrics
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - basic-tidb.tidb-cluster.svc.cluster.local:10080
        - basic-pd.tidb-cluster.svc.cluster.local:2379
# ---- Frappe, Saleor and Slack Spine ----
# The charts' own Prometheus is not deployed under SREGym; these jobs scrape the
# same targets it did. Targets of a namespace that is not deployed are simply down.
- job_name: 'incident-arena-slack-spine-app'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - svc-auth.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        - svc-workspace.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-channel.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-message.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-thread.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-file.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-search.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-notification.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
        - svc-platform.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8000
      labels:
        namespace: slack-spine
- job_name: 'incident-arena-slack-spine-services'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - ws-gateway.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:9101
        - flannel.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8200
        - channel-rt.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8201
        - dispatcher.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8202
        - presence.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8123
        - geodns.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8053
        - kafkagate.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8120
        - scheduler.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8121
        - search-engine.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:7280
        - db-maintenance.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8081
        - worker-index.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-unfurl.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-av.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-push.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-email.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-events.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-rollup.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - worker-retention.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:8122
        - postgres-exporter.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:9187
      labels:
        namespace: slack-spine
- job_name: 'incident-arena-slack-spine-envoy'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  metrics_path: /stats/prometheus
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - envoy-edge.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:9901
      labels:
        namespace: slack-spine
- job_name: 'incident-arena-slack-spine-redpanda'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  metrics_path: /public_metrics
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - redpanda.slack-spine.svc.cluster.local:9644
      labels:
        namespace: slack-spine
- job_name: 'workspace'
  scrape_interval: 10s
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
    - role: pod
      namespaces:
        names: [workspace]
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name]
      regex: metrics
      action: keep
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]
      target_label: namespace
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name]
      target_label: pod
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app]
      target_label: app
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_region]
      target_label: region
- job_name: 'incident-arena-frappe'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - mysqld-exporter.frappe.svc.cluster.local:9104
        - redis-exporter-cache.frappe.svc.cluster.local:9121
        - redis-exporter-queue.frappe.svc.cluster.local:9121
        - frappe-admin.frappe.svc.cluster.local:8000
      labels:
        namespace: frappe
- job_name: 'incident-arena-saleor'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets:
        - postgres-metrics.saleor.svc.cluster.local:9187
        - valkey-metrics.saleor.svc.cluster.local:9121
        - rabbitmq.saleor.svc.cluster.local:15692
      labels:
        namespace: saleor

alerting:
  alertmanagers:
  - kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
    tls_config:

    relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]

      regex: prometheus

    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app_kubernetes_io_name]
      regex: alertmanager
      action: keep
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_number]
      regex: "9093"
      action: keep

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
